newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to sell shares in Egypt Free Shops.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to sell shares in Egypt Free Shops.

text.p: An Egyptian state holding company said on Friday it is selling off 30 percent, or 1.05 million shares, in Egypt Free Shops, one of its wholly owned subsidiaries.

The holding company, Housing, Tourism and Cinema Company said in the statement published in al-Ahram newspaper that it is offering private investors 350,000 shares, investment funds and finance establishments and institutions 350,000, and the same number to workers.
The shares are priced initially at 32 pounds each. Private investors must buy at least 100 shares and institutional investors at least 1,000, it said.

Offers must be sent to National Bank of Egypt or brokerages from January 12, 1997 to January 13. The offers will be listed on the Cairo and Alexandria bourses from the 15th of the month to 1500 GMT on January 16 and the price of the shares adjusted within the limits set by the exchange, the statement said.

Egypt Free Shops, which has a monopoly on duty-free shops in Egypt, made profits for distribution of 13.423 million pounds ($3.95 million) in the financial year 1995/6, which ended on June 30. It forecast the 1996/7 figure would be 15 million.
The company has a paid-in capital of 35 million pounds, divided into 3.5 million shares with a nominal value of 10 pounds each.
